WHY: refreshHealth (health.ts:26-30) awaits each probe sequentially, so a refresh across unreachable-but-hanging upstreams is up to 3x slower than before, delaying the `upstream.healthy` transition that the fail-closed router (router.ts:8) relies on; with enough upstreams a refresh can also overlap the 30s interval that schedules it. HOW: either probe upstreams concurrently (e.g. `await Promise.all(list.map(async (u) => { u.healthy = await probeUpstream(u); }))`) or add a small backoff/cap so total probe time stays bounded.
verificationEvidence.rationale: The finding's mechanics are factually correct. With PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS=2000 and PROBE_RETRIES=2, probeUpstream loops attempt=0,1,2 and each hanging attempt costs the full 2s timeout before returning false, i.e. up to 6000ms for one unreachable-but-hanging upstream. refreshHealth (health.ts:26-30) awaits probes sequentially, so total refresh latency scales linearly and is 3x the pre-retry latency. router.ts:8 confirms the fail-closed path depends on `upstream.healthy`, and upstreams.ts:3 confirms a 30s refresh interval, so a large set of hanging upstreams can delay the healthy transition and even overlap the scheduling interval. The stated root cause, code path, and arithmetic all hold; no upstream guard caps or parallelizes the probes. No PreviousReviewDecisions entry concerns health.ts, so this is not a repeat.
